approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from a bounded population of accepted high-scoring molecules. It samples breeding parents by score band, recombines connected fragments and applies local graph mutations. Its retained special move exchanges a nitrogen and a carbon within one aromatic six-member ring, preserving formula and connectivity while changing nitrogen placement. Stable identity admission forms a fresh surplus pool. A Gaussian process trained on all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated score draws choose which pool members receive evaluations. Accepted offspring update both the prediction archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove only the direct aromatic nitrogen-position exchange from the atom-replacement menu and measure its contribution to the complete feedback loop. The ordinary element substitutions, crossover, other mutations and count-based posterior remain. Earlier evidence established useful positional edits before the posterior learned environment counts, and a later integration sibling removed crossover. None of the supplied siblings isolates whether this particular two-atom move still adds useful search paths under the retained count-based selector. Because some current exchange products improve incumbents and later breed, the registered prediction is a score decrease when the move is removed. The experiment tests that contribution rather than assuming sparse use makes the move dispensable.

hypothesis: Remove the direct formula-preserving aromatic C/N positional-exchange options from the inherited atom-replacement menu, leaving only its original single-atom element substitutions while retaining all other graph, feedback and posterior mechanisms.

finding_summary.headline: The same-code baseline reproduces all trajectories and the 0.595670 mean
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a complete baseline under the opening Research in Depth profile, with the exchange-free implementation and its feedback chain verified. Repeating the same seeds reproduced the same search histories; this adds execution and profile-baseline evidence without adding independent search trajectories or isolating any retained component’s value. The earlier finding that removing direct exchanges improved the mean remains a historical counterexample to the predicted loss, and is not retested here. The chemistry also reproduces the earlier limits: useful aromatic/carbonyl and aryl-amine arrangements coexist with reactive heteroatom–halogen bonds, doubtful ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Those liabilities and uneven task dispersion persist at the reproduced score. Current-profile component interventions are still needed to determine which retained mechanisms support that score and whether useful chemistry can be preserved while improving reliability.
finding_summary.results: All fifteen task runs completed. Final Top-1 macro mean was 0.595670, with seed population SD 0.026593; the three seed macros were 0.625412, 0.560866 and 0.600731. Every endpoint and every molecular trajectory reproduced the historical Anchor. Direct exchanges remained absent despite 904 eligible selected-site menus with 1,276 withheld partners. Accepted-only learning, crossover and correlated posterior selection all executed. The 4,350 accepted offspring produced 629 best-parent beats, 258 incumbent improvements and 2,401 later-used breeding molecules, exactly as before. The historical seeds are all profile-mismatched, so the protocol provides no paired effect estimate.

molecular.headline: The baseline reproduces aromatic heterocycles and aryl amines, including reactive halogen bonds and doubtful ring geometry
molecular.overall_character: This is the same-code profile baseline of Parent n-c55c3d520a2c, not a new chemical intervention. All supplied current and published Parent trajectory paths were present and read. Across all fifteen task/seed files, evaluation, source, SMILES, score and best_so_far records are identical to the Parent. The brief reports child_complete=true but paired_complete=false, no matched seeds, and profile-mismatched Parent seeds 0, 1 and 2. Thus the available historical chemistry comparison is exact reproduction; it is not a complete profile-matched Parent comparison, an independent chemistry sample, or evidence for any component contribution. The gaps below retain their original source in n-c55c3d520a2c and are re-observed in this baseline under its supplied Search Seeds and frozen profile. All five tasks are covered, each with 900 trajectory records and 870 optimizer proposals; no task lacks trajectories. The output comprises substituted indole amides and diketones, linked fused nitrogen heterocycles, flexible and cyclic aryl amines, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Ring-closure-string rates are 0.9632 to 0.9828 and aromatic-string rates are 0.954 to 0.9736. These are molecule-level incidences of text features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string rates are 0.0 throughout, although protonatable aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres are visibly present. Ring chemistry and aromaticity are rich, but synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because recognizable functional groups coexist with N-halogen and O-F bonds, peroxides, problematic cyclic unsaturation and difficult bridges. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with much narrower families among leaders within a seed; distinct SMILES alone do not establish independent scaffold coverage. Sizes below count heavy-atom tokens in the cited trajectory SMILES; SMILES lengths are the supplied digest counters. Neither those readings nor the supplied scores establish synthesis, stability, protonation, conformation or biological activity. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not the best retained molecule of every seed; the full trajectories were used to inspect other seed endpoints.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 molecule has 25 heavy atoms: an ethyl/dimethyl/chloro-substituted indole linked through an N-hydroxy amide to a pyridyl ring, with fluorine attached to the indole nitrogen. Nearby leaders keep the fused aromatic/amide/azaaryl organization while changing N-S, N-halogen or halomethyl substituents. Seed 2 develops an indole-aryl vicinal-diketone family with aminomethyl substitution; seed 0 also reaches an amino-substituted cumulene attached to a fused aromatic system. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.1 and halogen-string incidence is 0.8805. These are mostly compact aromatic frameworks rather than ring-deficient fragments, but their local nitrogen and halogen environments make apparently familiar skeletons questionable synthetic targets. The same families and exact scores occur in the published Parent.
liabilities: Leading N-F, N-Cl and N-Br attachments to indole nitrogen are chemically different from ordinary carbon-bound aromatic halogens; N-S substitution and halomethyl ethers also raise local reactivity concerns.
The N-hydroxy amide is a recognizable functional group but does not resolve the separate N-halogen liability on its scaffold.
The vicinal-dicarbonyl family has potentially reactive carbonyl chemistry, while the seed-0 leader contains a cumulated-double-bond segment; the scores do not demonstrate their stability.
missing_features: The leading examples do not establish conventional stable nitrogen substitution that preserves the favorable aromatic/carbonyl/azaaryl arrangement at the same score; an ordinary N-H indole amide is already present initially, so the generator is not incapable of that chemistry.
Chemically independent compact frameworks expressing the favorable functional-group arrangement are scarce among the leading examples; most vary substitutions on retained aromatic families.
The observed score ordering does not identify an exact missing pharmacophore, and does not establish that adding more donors, rings or halogens would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145, while the N-hydroxy pyridyl-amide leader reaches 0.47411701813450596. Retaining only an N-fluoro amide on the trimethoxyindole, without its pendant aryl group, gives 0.0038788336708218928; ClCl reaches 0.0. The visible positive association therefore concerns the combined compact aromatic and carbonyl organization, not halogen presence alone. Two N-halogen/halomethyl variants share 0.4478476056206344 despite different peripheral placements. The seed-2 diketone leader scores 0.438972502037081, whereas a more substituted late relative scores 0.2537139094300773; extra polar substitution is not uniformly rewarded. The seed-0 cumulene leader scores 0.39405142067435733. These comparisons do not isolate a required reactive bond or an absent target-specific motif.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader has 30 heavy atoms and links a quinazoline-like fused aromatic region to a dense nitrogen-rich fused/bridged carbonyl-thione core. It bears aryl chlorine, an O-F group, and a fluorinated chloromethyl-ether side chain. An analogue replaces that side chain with difluoromethyl. Seed 1 favors linked aza-aromatic and oxygen-containing carbonyl rings with a carbon-linked nitrile and an O-linked cyanate. Seed 2 instead reaches aryl/heteroaryl assemblies bearing peroxide, nitrite and N=S functionalities. Mean proposal SMILES length is 59.1, with a maximum of 191, so compact leaders coexist with much larger proposals. The recognizable fused heterocycles do not make their reactive attachments or dense ring junctions synthetically routine. These are the same output families as the Parent, with no baseline-specific change in size or chemistry.
liabilities: The leader contains an aryl O-F bond, not an aryl C-F bond, and a chloromethyl ether; these require a different reactivity assessment from ordinary aromatic halogen substitution.
Thione functionality and crowded nitrogen-ring connectivity coexist with unspecified stereochemical possibilities; a graph and score do not establish a synthetic route.

Other high-scoring seed families retain O-linked cyanates, peroxide links, nitrite and N=S groups. These are specific local chemistry concerns, not proof that all heterocycles or nitriles are undesirable.
missing_features: Stable peripheral alternatives that preserve the favorable linked heterocyclic arrangement are not established among the best examples; local substituent ties leave room for alternatives without identifying one as better.
The dense fused/bridged core lacks demonstrated accessible geometry and stereochemical identity; higher ring count alone does not recover the favorable arrangement.

The compact leading family appears in one seed while other seeds retain different reactive families; the observed record does not demonstrate reliable coverage of that favorable chemical organization across seeds.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.548381482770623, a smaller nitrogen-carbonyl ring fragment scores 0.5093370681605975, and ethene sits at 0.5. The linked nitrogen-rich leader and its difluoromethyl analogue both reach 0.8561477222467935. A nearby connectivity variant reaches 0.8467276542724114, while the more extensively cross-linked final seed-0 structure falls to 0.564499484004128. This favors a particular combined heterocyclic arrangement in this sample, rather than simply adding rings, atoms or fluorine. Other seed leaders reach 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013 in different families. The tied peripheral variants do not show that an O-F bond is required, and the floor score should not be interpreted as evidence of useful chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader is a 30-heavy-atom flexible tertiary amine connecting aromatic regions through alkyl chains, with phenol, methoxy, ethyl and propyl groups, a benzylic chloride and aromatic bromines. Seed 2 produces recognizable pyrrolidine-substituted dihydrobenzothiophene/biaryl frameworks with phenol or thiol and carbon-bound fluorine. Seed 1 favors an aminoethyl-substituted pyrrolidine attached to a fluorinated cyclic aryl-ether region with another aminomethyl group. Mean proposal SMILES length is 53.8 and halogen-string incidence is 0.9851. Accessible aliphatic amines and substantial aromatic surface are already present. These frameworks offer more recognizable synthetic handles than several other leading families, but heavy halogen substitution, flexible chains and unassigned stereochemistry remain concerns. The Parent contains the identical examples.
liabilities: The flexible leader combines a potentially reactive benzylic chloride with substantial bromine/chlorine mass and long hydrophobic alkyl segments; solubility, stability and selectivity are not characterized.
Some near-leading relatives introduce large ring closures or a cyclic cumulated-double-bond segment, whose feasibility is not established by their high scores.
The pyrrolidine and fused thioether skeletons are recognizable, but their unspecified stereochemistry prevents a fully defined molecular identity.
missing_features: Stereochemically specified forms of the successful saturated-ring and benzylic arrangements are absent, despite visible potential stereogenic centres.
A comparably evaluated stable replacement for the leading benzylic chloride is not established at its exact score; other high-scoring cyclic-amine families show that this liability is not universal.

Protonation states are not explicitly resolved in the neutral SMILES, but a lack of formal charge does not imply a lack of basic centres. The chemistry does not support a recommendation simply to add an amine.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An N-sulfonyl cyclic amine scores 0.00021169315013374197; the flexible tertiary amine reaches 0.9999989177995104 and the fused-thioether/pyrrolidine analogue 0.9999934235240012. A further aminoalkyl cyclic-amine leader reaches 0.9969753164881906. The visible association is the presentation of available aliphatic amines together with aromatic regions, rather than nitrogen or halogen count alone. A smaller final fused-thioether amine still scores 0.9947190867301007, so all aromatic appendages and maximal size are not required in this record. Flexible, cyclic and even cyclic-cumulene variants can approach the score ceiling. These are supplied oracle scores, not measurements of affinity, selectivity or geometric accessibility.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader has 29 heavy atoms and joins a propyl-substituted quinoline to a partially unsaturated, bridged nitrogen/oxygen ring system with N-methyl groups and carbonyls. Seed 1 uses related quinoline-linked amino/ether rings and dicarbonyl nitrogen rings; seed 0 reaches a densely bridged diaryl lactam containing an N-O bridge. Thus aromatic surfaces, saturated nitrogen centres and carbonyl acceptors are all represented. Mean proposal SMILES length is 52.6 and halogen-string incidence is 0.1241, much lower than in the other supplied families. Recognizable functional groups coexist with medium-ring bridges and difficult connectivity, so atom-count compactness alone does not establish an accessible synthesis. The same structures and gradients are already present in the Parent.
liabilities: Medium-ring closures, bridges and ring-bound unsaturation create synthesis and geometry questions despite moderate heavy-atom counts.

The diaryl leader contains an N-O bridge, and nearby variants introduce further N-O or N-N functionality; these require environment-specific assessment rather than treating all nitrogen substitutions as equivalent.
Stereocentre-string incidence is 0.0, so potential stereogenic saturated centres in these connected ring systems remain unspecified.
missing_features: The leading families do not demonstrate simpler, accessible connectivities that preserve the favorable arrangement of aromatic, nitrogen and carbonyl regions at the same score.
Stereochemical and conformational identity of the saturated bridges and medium rings is unresolved.
Chemically independent alternatives are limited among leaders within each seed, although the different seed families prevent a claim of total scaffold collapse.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329 and the leading quinoline/bridged-dicarbonyl structure reaches 0.22600312875247064. Extending its oxygen-containing ring segment gives 0.2243673789386108; a corresponding carbon-containing segment gives 0.22237557923837944. A different diaryl bridged lactam reaches 0.2258403994203931. These nearby values associate reward with the combined aromatic and nitrogen-carbonyl organization more than with a unique local atom. Methane scores 0.0. The final seed-2 bridged relative scores 0.20735848908965118, while its retained incumbent remains higher. The record supplies no exact missing target motif and no evidence that increasing general ring or heteroatom richness will solve the remaining gap.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader has 26 heavy atoms. It contains an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring bearing imino and carbonyl groups, N-fluoroalkyl substituents, and a fluorinated five-membered carbocycle with an enolic hydroxyl and a cumulated sequence of double bonds. This leader has carbon-bound fluorine rather than an N-F bond, but its cyclic cumulene raises a substantial geometric concern. Seed 0 instead retains N-fluorinated fused imino/carbonyl heterocycles attached to anisole and a small unsaturated nitrogen ring. Seed 1 retains a related fused dione with phenol and fluorinated alkenyl substituents. Mean proposal SMILES length is 46.6; the cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is 0.0517. Compact size and abundant nitrogen do not resolve the difficult ring geometry or reactive substitutions. All of this chemistry is reproduced from the Parent.
liabilities: The cumulated sequence forced into a five-membered ring raises severe strain and synthetic-accessibility concerns.

Other leaders retain N-F bonds and small unsaturated nitrogen rings. The top molecule's lack of N-F is a real counterexample to a universal N-F requirement, not evidence that local reactivity is controlled throughout the output.
A sharp local score change can occur while the doubtful core remains unchanged; score sensitivity therefore cannot certify that core's chemical feasibility.
missing_features: Geometrically credible alternatives preserving the compact fluorinated/polar organization are not established at the leading score; the high-scoring noncumulated relative is an important counterexample to any claim that reward requires the cyclic cumulene.

The large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring and enolic representation lack demonstrated conformational and tautomeric identity; lowercase aromatic notation is not evidence of a stable aromatic conformation.
Explicit stereochemical identity of substituted saturated centres is absent, and the scores do not identify an exact missing target pharmacophore or justify importing one.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-substituted fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. The cyclic-cumulene leader reaches 0.7208853668418119, while a related noncumulated carbocycle with changed nitrogen substitution reaches 0.6725143757617169. This is not an isolated cumulene comparison and does not show that the cumulene is required. The strongest close contrast changes the leader's N-fluoromethyl substituent to N-hydroxymethyl with the rest of the cited framework unchanged: the score falls to 0.006653135242129762. The observed sensitivity is to that local substitution within that scaffold, not a universal requirement for fluorine. Seed-0 and seed-1 leaders score 0.6510211907030741 and 0.4870057305679067 in other families. Isolated F and FF score 1.1043196211273875e-26 and 4.97400031457045e-24, respectively, so fluorination without molecular context is insufficient.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is reproduced identically in n-62daf219c70a on Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2 at 300 observations per task. Leaders contain N-F, N-Cl, N-Br, O-F, halomethyl ethers or benzylic chloride; other seed leaders contain peroxide and cyanate groups. Conventional carbon-bound halogens and recognizable tertiary or cyclic amines also occur at high scores, and one fluorinated leader contains no N-F bond. The problem is environment-specific, not an absence of heterocycles, amines or stable halogen chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional bond environments when modifying otherwise useful aromatic and heterocyclic frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs bond-environment-aware transformations and plausible local alternatives that retain favorable scaffold and functional-group relationships learned from feedback. Preserve ordinary carbon-bound halogens and useful nitrogen centres where supported. These structural associations do not establish that a universal filter or replacement raises the benchmark score, and the same-code baseline does not attribute the liability to a particular retained component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is reproduced identically in n-62daf219c70a on the supplied Search Seeds at 300 observations per task. The fluorinated imino/carbonyl leader combines a small cyclic cumulene with a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring; other leaders contain medium-ring bridges, and an aryl-amine relative contains cyclic cumulated double bonds. A noncumulated fluorinated relative and conventional saturated cyclic amines also have high scores, so neither unusual unsaturation nor difficult bridges are universal requirements.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish a representable ring graph from a geometrically credible unsaturation pattern or bridged topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction needs sensitivity to ring size, bond geometry and bridge connectivity, together with alternative topologies that preserve learned favorable functional arrangements. Ring counts and aromatic labels cannot supply this missing feasibility information. The observed families motivate assessing geometry, not a blanket prohibition of small rings, fused systems or ring formation; no causal score benefit is established here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was present in n-c55c3d520a2c and recurs without change in n-62daf219c70a across the supplied Search Seeds and observation budget. Every task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0, while the cited aryl/cyclic amines, fluorinated ring centres and bridged frameworks contain potentially stereogenic environments. Formal-charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but clearly protonatable amines are present; that is a separate representation question.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity after generating potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations need to preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemistry when a generated structure requires it, with appropriate treatment of achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Protonation and tautomerism should be assessed separately rather than inferred from the lack of charge markers. These records establish unspecified identity, not a measured stereochemical score penalty or a component-specific failure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and is reproduced identically in n-62daf219c70a on the supplied Search Seeds at 300 observations per task. Tiny halogen and hydrocarbon proposals reach observed floors, including late proposals, while useful scores occur for combinations of aromatic, carbonyl and amine regions. A more cross-linked final fused heterocycle scores below its compact leader. Conversely, a smaller fused-thioether amine retains a high score, so useful simplification is already possible and lower size is not intrinsically bad.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain enough functional-group context while avoiding unhelpful fragmentation and excessive elaboration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local feedback can inform transformations that preserve useful chemical context while simplifying or replacing dispensable portions. The missing capability is consistent control of context loss and elaboration, not an inability to make small molecules. Neither a fixed minimum molecular size nor an automatic preference for larger structures follows from these condition-dependent observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This gap was recorded for n-c55c3d520a2c and is re-observed in the identical n-62daf219c70a Search trajectories at the supplied budget. Leaders repeatedly alter halogen placement, short side chains, carbonyl-adjacent groups or ring segments on retained aromatic amide, fused heterocycle, aryl-amine and bridged dicarbonyl frameworks. Different seeds do produce different families, and ring-string incidence is high throughout, so the evidence supports limited leading-family alternatives rather than global structural collapse or inability to form rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently produce chemically independent plausible alternatives to the leading scaffold family within each seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Scaffold transformations should preserve learned favorable spatial and functional-group relationships while offering chemically independent, feasible connectivities. Evaluate whether such alternatives remain useful under task-local feedback; distinct strings alone do not establish useful scaffold coverage. This is a conditional chemical coverage gap, not evidence that any specific search component caused convergence or that more diversity necessarily improves the objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

Connected-fragment crossover with unchanged post-crossover mutation probability and multi-parent opportunities.

Verify exact announced batch receipts and canonical identities. On any common pre-divergence state compare unchanged parent allocation and posterior values; after changed menus change the graph RNG and feedback history, compare retained algorithms on their own contemporaneous valid inputs rather than demanding identical later populations. Every actual parent remains previously accepted and scored. Every posterior label remains finite, earlier and accepted in the same objective process; omitted exchanges and unselected pool alternatives never become training or breeding records.

Reconstruct eligible physical C/N pairs, selected-site partners, the exact ordered legacy numbers and the Parent numbers-plus-partners menu on that same source graph. Separate all-source eligibility, selected-site menu eligibility, empty legacy menus, symmetry-equivalent opportunities and later checker validity. Verify actual option_menu contains exactly the legacy integer choices, withheld_exchange_options contains exactly the sorted eligible partners, and the actual exchange selection probability is zero, versus len(partners)/(len(numbers)+len(partners)) in the inherited eligible menu. Confirm ordinary single-atom replacement and the other retained operators still execute, crossover still has actual multi-parent opportunities, and the count posterior still fits accepted data and selects through correlated masked draws. Existing parent evidence has 829 extended site menus and 435 actual valid exchanges; these are historical exposure counts, not required Child frequencies. Ordinary multistep substitutions may still produce a nitrogen positional isomer, so absence is a route-level claim and must not be inferred solely from final molecular structure.
activation_observables.name: For the registered removal or interaction, count eligible opportunities, confirm that the targeted mechanism is absent or altered, and verify retained mechanisms still activate at their declared interfaces.

activation_observables.measurement: Compare only the protocol-supplied matched complete Parent and Child per-task/per-seed final Top-1 endpoints, paired macro mean and dispersion using the supplied 0.002 meaningful-effect scale. The contribution prediction is a Child macro decrease of at least that scale after the direct route is removed; a smaller, null or positive effect fails to support that predicted contribution on this panel and does not imply nonexecution. Report all task and seed directions rather than using the pooled mean alone. Measure strict best-generating-parent beats, absolute offspring scores, child-minus-best-parent scores, incumbent increments, accepted-offspring reuse and later descendants, distinguishing one-parent and crossover cohorts. Reconstruct Parent clean-exchange versus mixed-edit histories and their descendant joins without assigning an individual swap the causal value of a later endpoint. Report typed and generic Murcko-core coverage under a fixed acyclic convention, actual size distributions, pool novelty/validity, retries, completion, observed graph/posterior time and full wall time. Passive withheld options have no counterfactual oracle scores. No speedup or smaller source claim follows from retaining enumeration and unreachable implementation for this controlled test.
activation_observables.name: Compare protocol-supplied matched per-seed and per-task final Top-1 outcomes, parent-beating yield, useful-core coverage and resource cost; distinguish observed comparative evidence from unscored same-pool decision probes.

activation_observables.measurement: Document unusual heteroatom bonds, large repeated assemblies, constrained rings, scaffold concentration and explicit versus unspecified stereochemistry in the actually emitted streams. Removing a formula-preserving move adds no chemical-quality gate and does not guarantee any direction for these incidences. Show task/seed score dispersion and distinguish loss of direct positional access from changed downstream family coverage or ordinary substitutions reaching similar products. Retain visible identity rejection, pool-exhaustion, saturation and numerical-fallback diagnostics and mark unexercised branches. Do not invent an evaluator stopping condition, infer molecular feasibility from valid canonical strings or attribute a specific task loss to an unscored omitted isomer.
activation_observables.name: Report residual reactive chemistry, stereochemical and scaffold limitations, score dispersion and unexercised numerical/exhaustion paths without treating them as proven failures or inventing a new stopping rule.

applicability_conditions: This is the single retained-mechanism removal permitted by the active integration_and_ablation Layer. Its graph and posterior interfaces remain unchanged, and the rest of each component stays at the supplied Parent implementation.

The removed route concerns neutral nonisotopic degree-two pyridine-like aromatic nitrogen and hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon within the same fully aromatic perceived six-member ring. Pyrrole-like/protonated nitrogen, substituted endpoints, arbitrary five-member moves and new atom-type restrictions are outside the experiment.

The changed menu affects both identity-changing and symmetry-identity direct exchanges because both are members of the retained route. Opportunity and use audits must separate those cases; source/formula conservation from historical exchanges is not a new guarantee for ordinary replacements.

The Parent's nine source-improving clean exchanges, four direct incumbent gains and later reuse motivate a decrease prediction, but the selected cohort is small and adaptive. Those observations do not prove that all exchange opportunities are useful or that any specific endpoint would be lost without them.

molecular_assessment.headline: The baseline reproduces aromatic heterocycles and aryl amines, including reactive halogen bonds and doubtful ring geometry
molecular_assessment.overall_character: This is the same-code profile baseline of Parent n-c55c3d520a2c, not a new chemical intervention. All supplied current and published Parent trajectory paths were present and read. Across all fifteen task/seed files, evaluation, source, SMILES, score and best_so_far records are identical to the Parent. The brief reports child_complete=true but paired_complete=false, no matched seeds, and profile-mismatched Parent seeds 0, 1 and 2. Thus the available historical chemistry comparison is exact reproduction; it is not a complete profile-matched Parent comparison, an independent chemistry sample, or evidence for any component contribution. The gaps below retain their original source in n-c55c3d520a2c and are re-observed in this baseline under its supplied Search Seeds and frozen profile. All five tasks are covered, each with 900 trajectory records and 870 optimizer proposals; no task lacks trajectories. The output comprises substituted indole amides and diketones, linked fused nitrogen heterocycles, flexible and cyclic aryl amines, bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Ring-closure-string rates are 0.9632 to 0.9828 and aromatic-string rates are 0.954 to 0.9736. These are molecule-level incidences of text features, not perceived ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string rates are 0.0 throughout, although protonatable aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres are visibly present. Ring chemistry and aromaticity are rich, but synthetic plausibility remains questionable and overall drug-likeness weak because recognizable functional groups coexist with N-halogen and O-F bonds, peroxides, problematic cyclic unsaturation and difficult bridges. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks, with much narrower families among leaders within a seed; distinct SMILES alone do not establish independent scaffold coverage. Sizes below count heavy-atom tokens in the cited trajectory SMILES; SMILES lengths are the supplied digest counters. Neither those readings nor the supplied scores establish synthesis, stability, protonation, conformation or biological activity. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not the best retained molecule of every seed; the full trajectories were used to inspect other seed endpoints.

per_task.generated_character: The leading seed-1 molecule has 25 heavy atoms: an ethyl/dimethyl/chloro-substituted indole linked through an N-hydroxy amide to a pyridyl ring, with fluorine attached to the indole nitrogen. Nearby leaders keep the fused aromatic/amide/azaaryl organization while changing N-S, N-halogen or halomethyl substituents. Seed 2 develops an indole-aryl vicinal-diketone family with aminomethyl substitution; seed 0 also reaches an amino-substituted cumulene attached to a fused aromatic system. Mean proposal SMILES length is 42.1 and halogen-string incidence is 0.8805. These are mostly compact aromatic frameworks rather than ring-deficient fragments, but their local nitrogen and halogen environments make apparently familiar skeletons questionable synthetic targets. The same families and exact scores occur in the published Parent.
liabilities: Leading N-F, N-Cl and N-Br attachments to indole nitrogen are chemically different from ordinary carbon-bound aromatic halogens; N-S substitution and halomethyl ethers also raise local reactivity concerns.
The N-hydroxy amide is a recognizable functional group but does not resolve the separate N-halogen liability on its scaffold.
The vicinal-dicarbonyl family has potentially reactive carbonyl chemistry, while the seed-0 leader contains a cumulated-double-bond segment; the scores do not demonstrate their stability.
missing_features: The leading examples do not establish conventional stable nitrogen substitution that preserves the favorable aromatic/carbonyl/azaaryl arrangement at the same score; an ordinary N-H indole amide is already present initially, so the generator is not incapable of that chemistry.
Chemically independent compact frameworks expressing the favorable functional-group arrangement are scarce among the leading examples; most vary substitutions on retained aromatic families.
The observed score ordering does not identify an exact missing pharmacophore, and does not establish that adding more donors, rings or halogens would help.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator needs bond-environment-aware transformations and plausible local alternatives that retain favorable scaffold and functional-group relationships learned from feedback. Preserve ordinary carbon-bound halogens and useful nitrogen centres where supported. These structural associations do not establish that a universal filter or replacement raises the benchmark score, and the same-code baseline does not attribute the liability to a particular retained component.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring construction needs sensitivity to ring size, bond geometry and bridge connectivity, together with alternative topologies that preserve learned favorable functional arrangements.
